Sources: [Wikipedia Celestiq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadillac_Celestiq), [KBB Celestiq](https://www.kbb.com/cadillac/celestiq/).

Price increase: starting at low-$400,000 range (up >$60,000 from 2025). Same 111-kWh battery, 655 hp dual-motor AWD, 303-mile range. Cadillac streamlined the design/order process. First sales year. Escalade IQ launched as a 2025 model in four trims: Luxury 1, Sport 1, Luxury 2, Sport 2. 205-kWh Ultium battery, dual-motor AWD producing 680 hp / 615 lb-ft (750 hp Velocity Max). EPA-estimated 460-mile range. Pricing from $127,700 (Luxury 1) to $148,200 (Sport 2). Sources: [Edmunds 2025 Escalade IQ](https://www.edmunds.com/cadillac/escalade-iq/2025/), [US News 2025 Escalade IQ](https://cars.usnews.com/cars-trucks/cadillac/escalade-iq/2025).

Four trims: Luxury ($132,695), Sport ($133,195), Premium Luxury ($152,995), Premium Sport ($153,495), all including $2,290 destination. First sales year for the Lyriq under the simplified Luxury 1/2/3 + Sport 1/2/3 trim ladder. Cadillac dropped the base Tech trim, cut pricing $2,000-$2,700 across the lineup. Starting MSRP $58,600 for Luxury 1 RWD; AWD adds ~$3,500. Up to 326 mile EPA range (RWD), 515 hp AWD / 365 hp RWD. Sources: [Edmunds 2025 Lyriq](https://www.edmunds.com/cadillac/lyriq/2025/), [KBB 2025 Lyriq](https://www.kbb.com/cadillac/lyriq/2025/).

Lyriq continues with refreshed trim structure. The high-performance Lyriq-V launches as a separate model. Standard Lyriq retains the Luxury/Sport tiering. Pricing for 2026 starts around $60,090 with Sport 3 at ~$68,990. Source: [Cars.com 2026 Lyriq pricing](https://www.cars.com/articles/how-much-is-the-2026-cadillac-lyriq-514245/), [Recharged 2026 Lyriq buying guide](https://recharged.com/articles/2026-cadillac-lyriq-buying-guide/).

All-new model variant for 2026. The Lyriq-V is the high-performance V-Series version of the Lyriq, with retuned dual motors (615 hp, 646 lb-ft), 3.3 second 0-60, 285 mile range, V-Series styling, performance brakes. Base MSRP $80,390, Premium trim above. Sources: [Edmunds 2026 Lyriq-V](https://www.edmunds.com/cadillac/lyriq/2026/v/), [KBB 2026 Lyriq-V](https://www.kbb.com/cadillac/lyriq-v/2026/specs/).

All-new model. The Optiq debuted for the 2025 model year as Cadillac's entry-level EV. Available in four trims: Luxury 1, Luxury 2, Sport 1, Sport 2 — all dual-motor AWD with an 85-kWh battery, 300 hp / 354 lb-ft, 302 mile range. Pricing from $52,895 (Luxury 1) to mid-$57Ks (Sport 2). Sources: [Edmunds 2025 Optiq](https://www.edmunds.com/cadillac/optiq/2025/), [CarGurus 2025 Optiq pricing](https://www.cargurus.com/research/articles/2025-cadillac-optiq-pricing-specs-release-date).

Major update for 2026: trim lineup expands to five (Luxury, Sport, Premium Luxury, Premium Sport, V-Series); a new single-motor RWD configuration arrives (315 hp, 332 lb-ft, 317 mile range); AWD now produces 440 hp / 498 lb-ft, 303 mile range; the Optiq-V tops the range at 519 hp Velocity Max, 278 mile range. The 2026 Optiq is the first Cadillac with a native NACS charging port (no adapter required for Tesla Superchargers). Pricing from $50,900 base to $68,795 for the V-Series. Sources: [Edmunds 2026 Optiq](https://www.edmunds.com/cadillac/optiq/), [Cadillac Laval — Optiq NACS](https://cadillaclaval.com/en/the-2026-cadillac-optiq-nacs).

All-new model for 2026. Four trims: Luxury ($77,395), Sport ($77,895), Premium Luxury ($91,895), Platinum ($96,495). 102-kWh Ultium battery, dual-motor AWD producing 615 hp / 650 lb-ft, 305-mile EPA range, 3.6 second 0-60. Super Cruise standard. 23-speaker AKG audio, panoramic sunroof, 33-inch curved infotainment display. Seating for six (captain's chairs) or seven (bench). 5,000 lb tow rating. Sources: [Edmunds 2026 Vistiq](https://www.edmunds.com/cadillac/vistiq/), [MotorWeek Vistiq](https://motorweek.org/road-tests/2026-cadillac-vistiq/).

2025 expanded trim availability and added the high-performance SS (615 hp Wide Open Watts mode, 0-60 in 3.4s, ~302 mi range). FWD LT added (broadest drivetrain choice in segment - FWD, RWD, AWD all offered across trims). Pricing held roughly flat vs 2024. Software issues from initial launch largely resolved. Sources: [Cars.com 2025](https://www.cars.com/research/chevrolet-blazer-ev-2025/), [Edmunds 2025](https://www.edmunds.com/chevrolet/blazer-ev/2025/).

For 2026, the rear-wheel-drive RS trim was discontinued; lineup now LT (FWD/AWD), RS (AWD only), and SS (AWD only). Small price increases (LT $44,600, RS $50,400, SS $60,600 - excluding destination). Range up to 312 mi (LT/RS FWD), 283 mi AWD, 302 mi SS. Carryover hardware. Sources: [Spitzer 2026 trims](https://www.spitzernorthfield.com/chevrolet-information/2026-chevy-blazer-ev-trim-levels-prices/), [KBB 2026](https://www.kbb.com/chevrolet/blazer-ev/).

2025 was the second model year for the Equinox EV. Trim structure simplified to LT and RS only (down from 1LT/2LT/3LT/2RS/3RS for 2024) with packages used to recreate higher-trim equivalents. FWD horsepower raised from 213 hp to 220 hp; AWD horsepower raised from 288 hp to 300 hp. EPA range up to 319 mi FWD / 285 mi AWD. Base price held near $34,995 including destination. Sources: [Cars.com 2025 Equinox EV intro](https://www.cars.com/articles/2025-chevrolet-equinox-ev-more-power-and-available-features-same-base-price-486275/), [Edmunds 2025 Equinox EV](https://www.edmunds.com/chevrolet/equinox-ev/2025/).

2026 reshuffles the trim ladder: now LT1, LT2, and RS (FWD and AWD on each LT trim; RS available FWD/AWD). Slight price increase across the lineup and destination freight raised from $1,395 to $1,800 (Dec 2025). Powertrain unchanged: 220 hp FWD / 300 hp AWD; 319 mi FWD / 307 mi AWD (AWD range slightly improved). New colors and small content tweaks; no battery / drivetrain hardware change. Sources: [Electrek 2026 Equinox EV preview](https://electrek.co/2025/10/07/2026-chevy-equinox-ev-gets-slight-price-bump-and-more/), [GM Authority 2026 pricing](https://gmauthority.com/blog/2025/08/here-is-2026-chevy-equinox-ev-pricing-with-options-and-packages/).

2025 added LT and RST consumer trims to the previously fleet-only WT lineup; expanded battery options (Standard Range ~270 mi, Extended Range up to 422 mi, Max Range up to 492 mi). RST First Edition $94,500 sold out and replaced by regular RST. Source: [GM Newsroom 2025 Silverado EV](https://news.gm.com/home.detail.html/Pages/news/us/en/2024/oct/1007-silveradoev.html).

2026 introduces the Trail Boss off-road trim (2-inch lift, 35-inch tires, Terrain drive mode, four-wheel steering). RST is sold only as the Stars & Steel Special Edition. Destination freight raised from $2,095 to $2,595 (Dec 2025) - $500 price uplift across lineup. Three new paint colors. Sources: [GM Newsroom Trail Boss](https://news.chevrolet.com/newsroom.detail.html/Pages/news/us/en/2025/may/0521-Trail-Boss-joins-2026-Chevrolet-Silverado-EV.html), [GM Authority 2026 pricing](https://gmauthority.com/blog/2025/06/here-is-2026-chevy-silverado-ev-pricing-with-options-and-packages/).

For 2025, Chrysler streamlined the Pacifica Hybrid trim lineup by discontinuing the Road Tripper and Premium S Appearance trims, leaving Select, S Appearance, and Pinnacle. Pricing held roughly flat with the prior year. Powertrain unchanged (16 kWh battery, 32-mile EV range, 82 MPGe, 260 hp combined). Uconnect 5 with 10.1-inch touchscreen and wireless CarPlay/Android Auto remained standard. Last full model year eligible for the $7,500 federal Clean Vehicle Credit when placed in service on or before September 30, 2025 (credit eliminated October 1, 2025 by the OBBBA). Sources: https://www.kbb.com/chrysler/pacifica-hybrid/2025/ ; https://www.edmunds.com/chrysler/pacifica/2025/plug-in-hybrid/ ; https://www.autoblog.com/deals/americas-only-plug-in-hybrid-minivan-loses-7500-tax-credit

MY2026 is the final production model year for the Pacifica Plug-in Hybrid as Stellantis discontinues the PHEV minivan and pivots away from PHEVs in North America. Trim lineup reshuffled: Select Premium replaces the prior S Appearance as the mid-tier trim, joining Select (entry) and Pinnacle (top). The mid-tier Select Premium adds ventilated Nappa leather seating, dual-pane panoramic sunroof, and integrated navigation. Pricing rose ~$2.7k on Select (now $53,760) and Pinnacle (now $62,460). Powertrain unchanged from 2025 (16 kWh battery, 32-mile EV range, 82 MPGe, 260 hp combined). Federal $7,500 Clean Vehicle Credit no longer available for MY2026 (eliminated October 1, 2025 by OBBBA). Sources: https://www.kbb.com/chrysler/pacifica-hybrid/ ; https://www.edmunds.com/chrysler/pacifica/2026/plug-in-hybrid/ ; https://www.cars.com/articles/stellantis-discontinues-chrysler-and-jeep-plug-in-hybrid-vehicles-520181/

MY2025 added the 4-door sedan body style (the MY2024 launched as 2-door coupe only); R/T and Scat Pack trims continued. R/T MSRP $54,930 (coupe); R/T AWD $57,995, Scat Pack AWD $64,995. Same 100.5 kWh (93.9 usable) battery and dual-motor AWD as MY2024. MY2025 caught both NHTSA recalls: instrument-cluster blank-out software fault (~20,271 units MY2024+MY2025 combined) and missing pedestrian-warning amplifier software (~8,390 units). Sources: https://carbuzz.com/cars/dodge/charger-daytona/2025/specs-and-trims/ ; https://www.cars.com/research/dodge-charger_daytona-2025/specs/ ; https://moparinsiders.com/stellantis-recalls-charger-daytona-ev-and-wagoneer-s-for-display-failure/

MY2026 cuts the entry-level R/T trim due to weak sales; only Scat Pack and a new luxury-oriented Scat Pack Plus remain, both in coupe and sedan bodies. MSRP starts at $61,990 (coupe Scat Pack) / $63,990 (sedan Scat Pack), with Scat Pack Plus topping out around $69,680. All 2026 Daytonas use the dual-motor 670 hp Scat Pack tune (630 hp standard, 670 hp with PowerShot, 3.3 second 0-60 mph). Scat Pack Plus adds a full-length glass roof, premium audio, and additional comfort tech. Battery and platform unchanged. Multi-energy Charger lineup adds the gasoline SIXPACK Charger variant for MY2026. The 2027 (not 2026) Daytona will be the first Stellantis EV with a factory NACS port. Sources: https://moparinsiders.com/2026-dodge-charger-daytona-buyers-guide-trims-pricing-specs-options-and-what-to-buy/ ; https://www.greencars.com/expert-insights/2026-dodge-charger-daytona-muscles-up-the-ev ; https://www.carsdirect.com/dodge/charger-daytona/2026

Final model year for the Hornet R/T PHEV (and the Hornet nameplate overall) — Stellantis announced January 2026 that Hornet production has ended, with no MY2026, attributing the discontinuation to the 25% imported-vehicle tariff under the Trump administration and a 54% YoY sales decline (82% Q4). MY2025 trims: R/T (MSRP ~$41,645) and R/T Plus (~$46,990). Same 1.3L turbo I4 + 90 kW e-motor + 15.5 kWh battery as prior years; 33 mi EV range, 77 MPGe combined, 288 hp PowerShot peak. Sources: https://www.autoblog.com/news/dodge-officially-kills-hornet ; https://electrek.co/2026/01/16/jeep-dodge-owner-kills-off-another-vehicle-over-us-policy-changes/ ; https://www.dodge.com/2025/hornet/specs.rt.html

Carryover MY relative to 2024; no major hardware changes. US MSRP held around $351,950 base. Same 7.45 kWh battery, ~15 mi electric range. Sources: https://www.cars.com/research/ferrari-296_gtb-2025/, https://www.kbb.com/ferrari/296-gtb/

Carryover MY; mild price adjustment. iSeeCars reports a 2026 base around $342,000 (some pricing variance across sources). The arrival of the 296 Speciale derivative for MY2026 fills the high-performance slot above the GTB. Carryover MY; same PHEV powertrain and retractable hardtop. US MSRP cluster around $376,000-$384,950 base depending on source. Sources: https://www.kbb.com/ferrari/296-gts/, https://www.cars.com/research/ferrari-296_gts-2025/

Carryover MY; arrival of the 296 Speciale A (Aperta) above it in the convertible lineup. No documented base GTS hardware refresh. Sources: https://www.classic.com/m/ferrari/296/gts/year-2026/, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_296

First MY for the 296 Speciale (announced April 2025). 36 hp more from the V6 ICE, e-motor liberated to 177 hp, 868 hp total. 60 kg lighter dry weight (1,410 kg). Aero upgrades, new active rear wing, race-tuned suspension. Sources: https://www.ferrari.com/en-EN/auto/296-speciale, https://www.topgear.com/car-reviews/ferrari/296-speciale

First MY for the 296 Speciale A (Aperta convertible). Shares the Speciale's aero panels and 868 hp combined PHEV powertrain; carbon-fiber retractable hardtop. Sources: https://www.encycarpedia.com/us/ferrari/25-296-speciale-aperta-convertible, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_296

Final production MY for the SF90 Spider. Same hardware as the closing-out Stradale; retractable hardtop adds ~100 kg. Sources: https://www.cars.com/research/ferrari-sf90_spider-2025/, https://www.jdpower.com/cars/2025/ferrari/sf90-spider

Final production MY for the base SF90 Stradale. Carryover hardware vs MY2024. 8 mi EPA electric range, 51 MPGe in EV mode, 18 MPG combined ICE per fueleconomy.gov. Final production year for the SF90 XX Spider (599-unit run completes). Same 1,030 hp combined PHEV powertrain and aero package as XX Stradale; carbon-fiber retractable hardtop. Sources: https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/ferrari/sf90_xx_spider/2025/2025-ferrari-sf90_xx_spider

Final production year for the SF90 XX Stradale (799-unit run completes). Carryover hardware: 1,030 hp combined PHEV powertrain, fixed rear wing, race-derived aero. Sources: https://carbuzz.com/cars/ferrari/sf90-xx-stradale/, https://rossoautomobili.com/blogs/ferrari-models/2023-ferrari-sf90-xx-stradale

MY2025 carried forward the MY24 powertrain (87 kW / 117 hp front motor, 42 kWh battery, 141-149 mi EPA range) and chassis unchanged. Trim lineup consolidated from MY24's three 'Inspired by' editions into a clearer two-tier structure: INSPI(RED) (base, only in Red by (RED) paint) at $32,495 and Icona (mid) at $34,745 — both originally announced. A range-topping Giorgio Armani Collector's Edition ($37,495, limited to 500 US units, Green or Greige only) was added with custom 17-in Armani wheels, leather, wood-grain trim, and laser-etched dash. Fiat applied a mid-cycle $2,000 MSRP cut across the lineup (announced early 2025, INSPI(RED) base re-aligned around $30,500 + $1,995 destination = $32,495 OTD). A $7,500 lease bonus cash incentive offset the lack of federal tax credit eligibility (Italian-built, ineligible under IRA NAFTA-assembly rule). Persistent slow sales — KBB / Carscoops reports of dealers offering $15,000 off — drove Fiat to simplify trims and raise prices for MY26.

MY2026 retains the same 42 kWh battery, 87 kW (117 hp) front motor, FWD layout, 141-149 mi EPA range, and ≤85 kW DC fast-charge peak as MY24/25. Notable changes: trim lineup simplified again to just Pop ($35,700) and Icona ($37,700) — Giorgio Armani Collector's Edition dropped. MSRPs rose substantially despite the MY25 mid-cycle cut (base up ~$5,200 from MY25 base of $30,500). Stellantis added Tesla Supercharger access via NACS-to-CCS1 adapter for all MY24-26 500e units (March 2026 announcement); the car itself still uses a native CCS1 port. US showroom arrival targeted summer 2026. No mechanical/battery refresh.

MY2025 Escape continues the post-2023 facelift design with six trims: Active (1.5L EcoBoost ICE-only), ST-Line, ST-Line Select, ST-Line Elite, Platinum (1.5L EcoBoost or 2.5L Hybrid, AWD optional on Hybrid), and PHEV (2.5L Atkinson + 14.4 kWh + electric motor, FWD-only, 37 mi EV range). 2.0L EcoBoost AWD remains available on ST-Line Elite and Platinum. SYNC 4 with 13.2-in touchscreen on higher trims. Hybrid trim mix is the principal electrified slice for MY2025 — Active does not offer hybrid in MY2025/2026. ST-Line Hybrid MSRP $32,490; ST-Line Select Hybrid +$995 vs gas; ST-Line Elite Hybrid $38,110; Platinum Hybrid $35,615; PHEV $39,895 (single trim). Sources: [Edmunds 2025 Escape PHEV](https://www.edmunds.com/ford/escape/2025/plug-in-hybrid/), [CarBuzz 2025 Escape](https://carbuzz.com/cars/ford/escape/2025/), [Bill Brown Ford 2025 PHEV specs](https://www.billbrownford.net/ford-escape/2025-escape-plug-in-hybrid-specs/).

MY2026 Escape is the **final model year**. US production ended Dec 2025 at Louisville Assembly; what's at dealers is what was built. Six trims continue (Active, ST-Line, ST-Line Select, ST-Line Elite, Platinum, PHEV) but **MY2026 Escape is not offered for sale in California, New York, Massachusetts, Vermont, Oregon, or Washington** — Ford declined CARB recertification for a final-year model. PHEV remains 14.4 kWh, 37 mi EV range, FWD-only, MSRP $35,400 + $1,495 destination = $36,895. National inventory is large (~11,000+ units). After 2026 Ford pivots fully away from Escape; no replacement announced. Sources: [Edmunds 2026 Escape PHEV](https://www.edmunds.com/ford/escape/2026/plug-in-hybrid/), [Jay Malone 2026 Escape trims](https://www.jaymaloneford.com/blog/2026/april/11/2026-ford-escape-trim-levels-active-st-line-st-line-select-st-line-elite-platinum-phev.htm), [AutoTechSpot - Escape discontinuation](https://autotechspot.com/car-updates/ford-escape-discontinued-2026), [Ford Authority - 2026 Escape packages](https://fordauthority.com/2025/10/2026-ford-escape-all-available-packages/).

MY2025 F-150 reflects the 14th-gen 2024 facelift refinements: revised front fascia, new digital instrument cluster on higher trims, 12-in standard touchscreen with SYNC 4 (15.5-in available). PowerBoost 3.5L Full Hybrid V6 (430 hp / 570 lb-ft, ~24 mpg combined) available on most trims XLT and above. Pro Power Onboard standard with PowerBoost up to 7.2 kW (2.4 kW base; 7.2 kW upgrade). 12,700 lb max tow with PowerBoost properly equipped. BlueCruise 1.x hands-free available on Lariat and above (subscription required after 90-day trial). Sources: [Ford.com 2025 F-150](https://www.ford.com/trucks/f150/2025/), [Edmunds 2025 F-150](https://www.edmunds.com/ford/f-150/).

MY2026 expands PowerBoost availability — now offered on STX, XLT, Lariat, King Ranch, and Platinum (more trims than 2025). Key drivetrain shift: 4x2 now available on Lariat, King Ranch, and Platinum, lowering base MSRP several thousand dollars on those trims versus 2025. PowerBoost premium over the 3.5L EcoBoost is $1,340. MSRPs: XLT $44,695, Lariat $59,560, King Ranch $65,825, Platinum $68,800 (gas-engine base; add $1,340 for hybrid). Combined output 430 hp / 570 lb-ft retained. Pro Power Onboard up to 7.2 kW remains. Sources: [Ford.com 2026 F-150](https://www.ford.com/trucks/f150/), [Edmunds 2026 F-150 Hybrid](https://www.edmunds.com/ford/f-150/2026/hybrid/), [AutoFair Haverhill 2026 F-150 review](https://www.autofairfordofhaverhill.com/new/ford/f-150/offer.htm).

Five-trim MY2025 lineup: Pro (fleet/retail), XLT, Flash, Lariat, Platinum. Standard Range 98 kWh battery on Pro/XLT/Lariat with up to 240 mi range; Extended Range 131 kWh on Flash/Platinum (standard) or optional on XLT/Lariat, up to 320 mi (300 mi on Platinum with 22-in wheels). Tesla Supercharger access via NACS adapter. Production paused for six weeks Nov 18 2024 - Jan 6 2025 (originally), then **paused indefinitely from Oct 2025** after a Novelis aluminum plant fire and citing better profitability on gas/hybrid F-150. MY2025 inventory continues at US dealers as of May 2026. Sources: [Edmunds 2025 Lightning](https://www.edmunds.com/ford/f-150-lightning/), [US News 2025 Lightning](https://cars.usnews.com/cars-trucks/ford/f-150-lightning), [Ford.com 2025 Lightning](https://www.ford.com/trucks/f150-lightning/).

MY2026 changes: 98 kWh Standard Range battery discontinued — 123 kWh (extended) is now standard across the line; XLT trim replaced by new off-road STX (e-locking rear diff, Tremor-style running boards, all-terrain tires, unique wheels). Pro restricted to Fleet Only. MSRP cuts on Flash and Platinum vs. MY2025. **Production indefinitely paused since Oct 2025** at the Rouge EV Center; workers transferred to adjacent Dearborn Truck Plant for ICE F-150 production. Limited 2026 inventory at dealers — what was built prior to the halt. Sources: [Ford Authority - 2026 Lightning trim cuts](https://fordauthority.com/2025/10/2026-ford-f-150-lightning-msrp-cut-for-two-trims/), [Bowen Scarff 2026 Lightning](https://www.bowenscarff.com/2026-ford-lightning-factory-order/), [TrueCar 2026](https://www.truecar.com/overview/ford/f-150-lightning/2026/).

MY2025 brings a major mid-cycle refresh: new front-end styling, revamped interior with 13.2-in touchscreen running SYNC 4, redesigned dash and gauge cluster. New trim structure replaces XL/XLT/Lariat with: XL, XLT, Lariat, plus performance-focused Lobo and off-road Tremor (both EcoBoost-only). Sources: https://karmaautomotive.com/revero/, https://www.karmawestfield.com/new-inventory/karma-revero.htm

Carryover. Same four trims, ~$190 MSRP increase across the board, no equipment changes. LXS $40,990 / EX $43,190 / SX Prestige $53,090. 33 mpg combined. Source: https://www.autoblog.com/news/2026-kia-carnival-only-gets-a-tiny-price-increase-should-you-buy-a-2025-instead

GT performance variant retained at 601 hp / 0-60 in 3.4 s. Sources: https://evchargingstations.com/chargingnews/2026-kia-ev6-lower-msrp/ , https://www.kiamedia.com/us/en/models/ev6/2025

Standard NACS port and CCS1-to-NACS DC fast-charge adapter included (ZEV states). Sources: https://evchargingstations.com/chargingnews/2026-kia-ev6-lower-msrp/ , https://carbuzz.com/2026-kia-ev6-pricing-announced/

CCS1 charging port; NACS adapter program for free if delivered after 2024-09-04. Same E-GMP platform, same 76.1 kWh / 99.8 kWh battery options. Source: https://www.kbb.com/kia/ev9/2025/specs/

Up to $2,000 price reductions on some trims; range improvements on select trims. AWD trims gained a new Terrain mode replacing prior four-wheel-drive mode. Source: https://evchargingstations.com/chargingnews/nacs-equipped-2026-kia-ev9-pricing-emerges/ , https://invoice-pricing.com/cars/news/the-2026-kia-ev9-gets-a-nacs-charging-port-and-the-nightfall-edition/

Larger 10.25-inch instrument cluster (formerly 4.2-inch analog), rotary dial transmission controller, light option pack changes. Wind / Wave trims carry over. $39,600 / $44,600 starting MSRPs. Carryover MY. Wind / Wave trims continue. Kia NACS adapter program continues — $249 at dealers for Niro EV owners. No major hardware refresh. Sources: https://www.kia.com/us/en/niro-ev , https://www.kia.com/us/en/niro-ev/build

Two trims (EX FWD/AWD-optional, SX Prestige AWD). 1.6T-hybrid powertrain, 227 hp / 258 lb-ft. EX FWD 36 mpg combined; AWD 34 mpg combined. SX Prestige AWD MSRP ~$53,090.

Three trims (EX, X-Line, SX Prestige). X-Line appearance package made standard on top trims. Sorento Hybrid base price $40,335. EX FWD 37 mpg combined / 655 mi total range. No major powertrain changes. Source: https://www.kiamedia.com/us/en/media/pressreleases/23688/kia-announces-pricing-for-2026-sorento-hev
Two trims (EX, SX Prestige). EX $49,365; SX Prestige $54,465. 261 hp, 32 mi EV range, 74 MPGe combined.

Two trims (EX, X-Line SX Prestige — the latter renamed from MY2025 SX Prestige with X-Line appearance package now standard). Base price $49,735 incl. destination — only $300 above MY2025. 261 hp, 31 mi EV range (~1 mi reduction), 440 mi total range, 33 mpg combined hybrid mode. Source: https://www.cars.com/research/kia-sorento_plug_in_hybrid-2026/

Three trims (LX FWD/AWD, EX AWD, SX Prestige AWD). LX from $30,185. 1.6T-hybrid powertrain 227 hp / 258 lb-ft. LX FWD 43 mpg combined; EX/SX Prestige AWD 38 mpg combined. Source: https://www.kbb.com/kia/sportage-hybrid/2025/

Mid-cycle facelift: stacked LED headlight design, restyled front/rear bumpers, new wheels, standard 12.3-inch infotainment. Two new trims added (S and X-Line) for a total of five (LX, S, EX, X-Line, SX Prestige). LX from $30,490. Powertrain bumped to ~232 hp. S adds heated seats and BSW; X-Line is appearance package w/ 19-inch wheels. Two trims (X-Line, X-Line Prestige). 261 hp combined, 34 mi EV range, standard AWD. X-Line Prestige MSRP ~$45,960. Source: https://www.kiamedia.com/us/en/models/sportage-phev/2025/specifications

Same two trims (X-Line, X-Line Prestige). MY2026 bumps combined output to 268 hp / 271 lb-ft via 7-hp electric-motor boost; retains 34 mi EV range. Two NHTSA recalls landed on MY24/MY25 units during the MY25 sales window (Jul 2025 door gas-spring pin torque on 27 US units; Jan 2026 rearview-camera software defect). Sources: https://www.cars.com/research/lamborghini-revuelto-2025/ , https://www.cars.com/research/lamborghini-revuelto/recalls/

Slots above the (still-sold) Urus S, below where the Performante used to sit. value.refreshNotes: First model year of the 48V mild-hybrid Outlander in the US — replaces the prior 2.5L naturally-aspirated I4 with a new Mitsubishi-designed 1.5L turbocharged I4 paired with a 48V BSG mild-hybrid system. Combined output 174 hp / 206 lb-ft (torque up 25 lb-ft vs. 2025's 2.5L). EPA-estimated 28 MPG combined. New LE trim sits between ES and SE (adds adaptive cruise, 20-inch black wheels, faux-leather seats, multi-view camera, wireless charger). Base ES MSRP $29,995 FWD / $31,795 S-AWC (with destination ~$31,740). Trail Edition and RALLIART appearance trims at $39,295 MSRP. Black Edition tops the lineup near $44,790. Mid-cycle update of the 4th-gen Outlander PHEV (carried over from MY2024 with minor packaging/option tweaks). Continues with 20.0 kWh battery, 38-mile EPA all-electric range, 248 hp combined system output, 64 MPGe combined, and twin-motor S-AWC AWD standard on every trim. Six trims sold (ES, SE, SEL, SEL Premium, SEL Black Edition, SEL Platinum). CHAdeMO DC fast charging remains an upper-trim feature. The 2025 model year is the final year of the original 4th-gen battery spec before the 2026 22.7 kWh refresh. Interior updates: revised seat materials, cooled front seats on select trims, redesigned cupholders, larger armrest storage, new phone-charging pad, optional 12-speaker Yamaha Dynamic Sound audio (8-speaker base). value.refreshNotes: For MY25 in the US, Polestar drastically pruned the lineup to a single fully-loaded variant: Long Range Dual Motor with the Performance Pack standard. The previous separate Single Motor and base Dual Motor trims were dropped. The car otherwise carried over the MY24 hardware refresh (82 kWh battery, rear-biased dual-motor layout, 205 kW DC peak charging). Sources: https://carbuzz.com/cars/polestar/2/2025/, https://www.polestar-forum.com/threads/us-2025-polestar-2-fully-loaded-with-performance-pack-only.15052/, https://recharged.com/articles/2025-polestar-2-buying-guide

Inaugural MY for the Polestar 3 in the US. Three trims: Long Range Single Motor (RWD, 295 hp, 315 mi EPA range), Long Range Dual Motor (AWD, 489 hp, 279 mi), and Long Range Dual Motor with Performance Pack (AWD, 517 hp, 279 mi). A Launch Edition was offered early in the run with extras at higher MSRP. 400V electrical architecture, 250 kW DC fast charging peak, 10-80% in ~30 min. Sources: https://www.edmunds.com/polestar/3/, https://www.kbb.com/polestar/3/2025/specs/, https://www.evspecifications.com/en/model/3aca43a

Major mid-cycle refresh in only the model's second year: switch from 400V to 800V electrical architecture, peak DC fast charging raised from 250 kW to 350 kW (310 kW on rear-motor trim), 10-80% now ~22 min (down from ~30 min). Output bumped across the board: Rear Motor 333 hp (was 295), Dual Motor 544 hp (was 489), Performance 680 hp (was 517). Trim names simplified to Rear Motor / Dual Motor / Performance. Active air suspension newly available on Dual Motor. NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Orin processor replaces prior compute, claimed ~8x AI processing uplift (30 -> 254 TOPS) — relevant to future ADAS feature additions via OTA. New Climate and Prime option packs introduced. Sources: https://carbuzz.com/2026-polestar-3-updates/, https://www.autoblog.com/news/2026-polestar-3-updates, https://www.carsdirect.com/polestar/3/2026

Inaugural US model year for the Polestar 4 (orders opened June 2025, deliveries fall 2025). US-market cars assembled in South Korea (Renault Korea / Busan) rather than China to mitigate US import tariff exposure. Three trims offered: Long Range Single Motor (RWD, 268-272 hp, 310 mi EPA range), Long Range Dual Motor (AWD, 544 hp, 280 mi), and Dual Motor with Performance Pack ($4,500 add-on: 22-in wheels, ZF active dampers, Brembo brakes, Swedish gold accents; 544 hp, 255 mi). 94 kWh battery, 200 kW DC peak (10-80% in ~30 min). Most distinctive feature: no rear window — replaced by roof-mounted high-resolution rear camera feeding a digital interior mirror. Sources: https://www.polestar.com/us/polestar-4/specifications/, https://blog.consumerguide.com/2026-polestar-4-review-prices-and-specs/, https://electrek.co/2025/06/03/2026-polestar-4-officially-on-sale-us-priced-slightly-higher/

First model year for the T-Hybrid powertrain in the 911. Launches in 4 GTS body variants: Coupe RWD, Cabriolet RWD, Carrera 4 GTS Coupe AWD, Targa 4 GTS AWD. New single-turbo 3.6L flat-six (replacing twin-turbo 3.0L on GTS), 400V mild-hybrid system with electric exhaust turbo and PDK-integrated motor. 532 hp / 449 lb-ft combined. 0-60 ~2.9 sec. Refreshed digital cockpit (all-digital cluster, no analog tach for the first time ever in a 911). Source: https://newsroom.porsche.com/en_US/products/911/new-911-carrera-gts-t-hybrid-35857.html

T-Hybrid GTS lineup carries over. New 911 Turbo S T-Hybrid debuts for MY2026 (officially revealed late 2025), bringing the T-Hybrid system to the 911 Turbo S with substantially higher output (~700+ hp combined). Carrera GTS variants continue with carryover specs and minor MSRP increases. Source: https://www.porsche.com/usa/models/911/

Continuation of 2024 mid-cycle refresh. PHEV lineup: Cayenne E-Hybrid ($96,300), Cayenne S E-Hybrid ($101,400, MY24+), Cayenne Turbo E-Hybrid ($150,300). Coupe variants priced ~$5-8k above SUV equivalents. Larger 25.9 kWh battery (vs prior 17.9 kWh), 11 kW AC charger. New Porsche Driver Experience dash (12.6" curved cluster + 12.3" center + optional 10.9" passenger display). Driver-attention camera new for 2024+. Source: https://newsroom.porsche.com/en_US/products/cayenne/cayenne-2024-update-32841.html

Carryover MY26. Minor MSRP increases. Next-gen Cayenne BEV launches alongside late 2026 but the PHEV/ICE Cayenne continues in parallel for several more years. Same PHEV lineup (E-Hybrid, S E-Hybrid, Turbo E-Hybrid) in SUV and Coupe bodies. Source: https://www.porsche.com/usa/models/cayenne/

Macan 4S ($86,200) added late 2024 as a mid-lineup addition. EPA-rated range up to 308 mi (Macan RWD). New Porsche Driver Experience cabin layout (curved 12.6" driver display + 10.9" center + optional 10.9" passenger display + augmented-reality HUD optional). Driver-attention camera standard. Third-generation Panamera continues into its second full MY in the US. PHEV trims: 4 E-Hybrid, 4S E-Hybrid (new for G3), Turbo E-Hybrid, Turbo S E-Hybrid. Major changes vs G2: larger 25.9 kWh battery, ~32 mi EPA EV range, 11 kW AC charger, new Porsche Active Ride active hydraulic suspension (optional), Porsche Driver Experience cabin layout. Carryover MY26. Minor MSRP and option-package adjustments. Same PHEV lineup: 4 E-Hybrid, 4S E-Hybrid, Turbo E-Hybrid, Turbo S E-Hybrid. Source: https://www.porsche.com/usa/models/panamera/

Major mid-cycle refresh ('Gen 1.5'). Larger Performance Battery Plus (105 kWh gross / 97 kWh usable, up from 93.4/83.7), new rear permanent-magnet motor (PSM), updated pulse-controlled inverter, regen capped at 400 kW (up from 290 kW), DC fast-charge peak 320 kW (up from 270 kW), 10-80% in ~18 min, 800V on-board charger increased to 11/22 kW AC. EPA range gains: base Taycan RWD up to 318 mi (from 242). Power increases across the lineup (Turbo S now 938 hp with launch control overboost). New driver-attention camera (gaze tracking) standard. New Push-to-Pass (PTP) overboost on Turbo S/Turbo GT. Infotainment updates: passenger display now available, new HVAC controls. Turbo GT new for 2025 ($231,995 USD), the most powerful production Porsche ever, sedan-only or with Weissach Package. Sport Turismo wagon returns to US lineup for 2025.

The 2025 Ram 1500 received a major mid-cycle refresh of the DT-generation platform. Key changes: (1) revised front-end styling with new grille and LED headlights; (2) updated interior with new dashboard and standard 12-inch touchscreen on most trims, optional 14.5-inch on higher trims; (3) the 3.0L Hurricane twin-turbo inline-six engine family replaced the 5.7L HEMI V8 in the standard lineup — Hurricane SO (420hp/469 lb-ft) and Hurricane HO (540hp/521 lb-ft); (4) introduction of the new range-topping Tungsten trim with HO Hurricane standard and four-corner air suspension; (5) introduction of the RHO trim replacing the discontinued TRX; (6) discontinued legacy TRX; (7) 3.6L Pentastar V6 eTorque continues as base engine on Tradesman and Big Horn. The Hurricane I6 includes a 48V mild-hybrid belt-starter-generator system. Both 5.7L HEMI V8 eTorque and 6.2L supercharged HEMI V8 (TRX) were discontinued for 2025 — the HEMI returns for 2026. The 2026 Ram 1500 carries forward the 2025 refresh with two major changes: (1) The 5.7L HEMI V8 with eTorque mild-hybrid returns as an option on Tradesman, Big Horn, Express, Warlock, Laramie, Rebel (late availability), Limited, and Longhorn trims — Ram brought back the V8 in response to customer demand after dropping it from the 2025 lineup. The 5.7L HEMI V8 eTorque is rated at 395 hp and 410 lb-ft of torque. On Limited and Longhorn it is offered as a no-charge upgrade; on Big Horn it adds approximately $2,895 to the MSRP. (2) Lineup adjustments: the 'Tradesman HFE' designation was dropped; an 'Express' value-trim was added; the 'Limited Longhorn' was simplified to 'Longhorn'. (3) Slight base-MSRP increase: Tradesman base MSRP moved from $42,270 (2025 with destination) to about $42,025 base + $2,595 destination for 2026. All-new model year: first 2026 Crosstrek Hybrid, replacing the long-discontinued PHEV variant (MY2019-2023). Uses next-gen Toyota-derived hybrid system shared with the Forester Hybrid: 2.5L Atkinson/Miller BOXER + electric motors + Symmetrical AWD via CVT, 194 hp combined. EPA-estimated ~36 mpg combined, ~600 mi total range. Two trims: Sport Hybrid ($33,995) and Limited Hybrid ($36,990) [https://media.subaru.com/pressrelease/2335/subaru-announces-pricing-2026-crosstrek-including-new-2026]. Maintains gas-Crosstrek 8.7 in ground clearance. Standard wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, EyeSight driver assist. Arrived at retailers fall 2025.

All-new model: first hybrid Forester ever sold in the US. Built on the new 6th-gen Forester platform with the next-generation Subaru/Toyota hybrid system (2.5L Atkinson-cycle BOXER + electric motors + Symmetrical AWD via CVT, 194 hp combined). EPA-estimated ~35 mpg combined, ~581 mi total range, ~40% better city MPG vs gas Forester. Four trims at launch: Premium, Sport, Limited, Touring. Started arriving at dealers end of April 2025; pricing from $36,595 MSRP base Premium to $43,295 Touring [https://media.subaru.com/pressrelease/2280/1/subaru-announces-pricing-new-2025-subaru-forester-hybrid]. Standard EyeSight driver assist, 11.6-inch portrait touchscreen, 12.3-inch digital cluster.

Carry-over with revised pricing. Same 2.5L BOXER + hybrid powertrain (194 hp combined), Symmetrical AWD via CVT, ~35 mpg combined, ~581 mi total range. Four trims: Premium ($36,180 incl. $1,450 destination), Sport, Limited ($38,995), Touring ($41,545) [https://media.subaru.com/newsrelease.do?id=2424]. No major hardware changes: still 72.8 kWh battery, dual 80 kW motors, 215 hp combined, ~222-227 mi EPA range, CCS1 charging (max ~100 kW DCFC). Trim lineup: Premium, Limited, Touring, Touring Onyx Edition. Tesla Supercharger access added via SubaruConnect app starting October 2025 using a Subaru-supplied NACS adapter [https://media.subaru.com/newsrelease.do?id=2384]. Lease-credit pathway: $7,500 commercial-clean-vehicle credit applied to lease payments through Subaru Motors Finance, available until 9/30/2025.

Trim restructure: Premium, Limited, Limited XT, Touring XT, Touring XT Leather. MSRP holds steady: Premium $38,495 (same as MY2025) [https://media.subaru.com/newsrelease.do?id=2376]. Federal new-vehicle EV tax credit expired 9/30/2025 — no federal tax credit available for MY2026 retail purchases.

Dual-motor Symmetrical AWD, 375 hp combined, 0-60 mph in 4.4 sec, 3,500 lb towing capacity, 8.5 in ground clearance. 74.7 kWh battery, EPA-estimated up to ~260 mi range, 150 kW DC fast charge (10-80% in ~28 min), native NACS (J3400) port with Tesla Supercharger access. 14-inch center touchscreen. Three trims: Premium ($39,995), Limited ($43,995), Touring ($46,555) [https://media.subaru.com/pressrelease/2397/1/all-new-2026-subaru-trailseeker-combines-375-horsepower]. On sale early 2026. Federal new-vehicle tax credit not applicable post 9/30/2025.

Premium trim is FWD-only (221 hp), the first FWD Subaru vehicle in the US in many years; Sport and GT trims add a rear motor for AWD (338 hp combined). 74.7 kWh battery, EPA-estimated range up to ~308 mi (Premium FWD) down to ~273 mi (GT), 10-80% DC fast charge in ~28 min via native NACS port. Class-leading 8.2 in ground clearance for the segment. For 2025 the US lineup consolidated to the 82 kWh Pro / Pro S / Pro S Plus trims (the 62 kWh Standard / S trims sold in MY2023-2024 were dropped). Pro RWD: 282 hp (up from 201 hp in earlier MY2023 RWD), 291 mi EPA range. AWD: 335 hp, 263 mi EPA range. Pro S Plus is AWD-only. Continues to be built in Chattanooga, TN and remains eligible for the full $7,500 federal tax credit. CCS1 charging port; NACS-to-CCS1 adapter sold as a $235 accessory but Tesla Supercharger access via VW was not formally opened until the MY2026 release. Sources: https://www.edmunds.com/volkswagen/id4/2025/ ; https://recharged.com/articles/2025-vw-id4 ; https://www.kbb.com/volkswagen/id4/2025/specs/

The big 2026 change is standard inclusion of a VW-branded NACS-to-CCS1 DC adapter, granting access to ~25,000 Tesla Superchargers from day one. AWD output bumped slightly (still 335 hp combined, but updated software / cooling). Lineup remains Pro (RWD or AWD), Pro S (RWD or AWD), Pro S Plus (AWD only). Base MSRP rose roughly $5,100 vs MY2025 according to CarsDirect: Pro $45,095, Pro S $50,195, Pro S Plus $57,655 (excluding the $1,475 destination fee). 12.9-inch touchscreen and IQ.DRIVE remain standard. 2-year Electrify America Pass+ with Plug & Charge included. Sources: https://www.carsdirect.com/automotive-news/2026-volkswagen-id-4-base-price-increasing-5-100 ; https://media.vw.com/releases/1891 ; https://www.vw.com/en/models/id-4.html ; https://www.cars.com/articles/how-much-is-the-2026-volkswagen-id-4-519597/

US-market launch year for the ID. Buzz. Long-wheelbase 3-row 7-seater spec unique to North America (Europe gets a shorter wheelbase, in addition to the long one). All trims: 91 kWh battery, 200 kW DC fast-charge peak (10-80% in ~26 min). RWD Pro S = 282 hp / 234 mi EPA range; Pro S Plus RWD = 282 hp / 234 mi; AWD variants = 335 hp dual motor / 231 mi. 1st Edition adds panoramic electrochromic glass roof and bespoke exterior styling. NHTSA 5-star overall. IIHS Good in moderate overlap front (AEB and headlights cited as weak points). Sources: https://media.vw.com/releases/1894 ; https://www.edmunds.com/volkswagen/id-buzz/2025/mpg/ ; https://recharged.com/articles/vw-id-buzz-safety-rating-crash-test

EC40 returns to the US market for MY2026 after skipping MY2025 — the model was renamed from C40 Recharge as part of Volvo's BEV naming refresh. Mechanically the EC40 is the EX40 with a fastback roofline. Same CMA platform, same Single Motor / Twin Motor powertrain options. Source: https://www.kbb.com/volvo/ec40/, https://www.cars.com/research/volvo-ec40-2025/

First US model year for the EX30 (Belgium-built after the China-tariff redirect). US shipments limited to Twin Motor Performance only — Single Motor Extended Range delayed. MSRP for the Twin Motor Performance starts around $46,600. Sources: https://insideevs.com/news/702527/2025-volvo-ex30-range-specs-pricing/, https://www.cars.com/research/volvo-ex30-2025/

Final US model year — Volvo announced in March 2026 it would stop US EX30 sales at end of MY2026, with final orders due by March 20, 2026. MY2026 brings the Single Motor Plus to the US (~$38,950 MSRP, 261 mi EPA) and the EX30 Cross Country Twin Motor Performance (227 mi EPA, ~$48,950). Sources: https://www.wardsauto.com/news/volvo-ends-EX30-sales-us-2026/815160/, https://www.motorcarsvolvocars.com/volvo-electric-models.htm

First year under the new EX40 name (formerly XC40 Recharge). Core, Plus, and Ultra trims, each with Single Motor (RWD, 248 hp, ~296 mi) or Twin Motor (AWD, 402 hp, ~254 mi). MSRP $53,795–$60,295 including destination. Comes with NACS adapter for Tesla Supercharger access. Source: https://www.cars.com/research/volvo-ex40-2025/trims/

MY2026 carries the EX40 forward with a built-in NACS port (no adapter needed for Tesla Supercharger DC-fast access on most trims) and ongoing OTA UX updates to the Volvo Car UX / Google Built-in stack. Trim structure unchanged (Core / Plus / Ultra × Single Motor / Twin Motor). Source: https://www.volvocars.com/us/cars/ex40-electric/

EX90 ramped through 2025 with ongoing OTA software waves to enable features that shipped disabled at the 2024 launch (wireless Apple CarPlay, full Pilot Assist, bidirectional charging marketing). Twin Motor and Twin Motor Performance available. NACS adapter included as standard with MY2025 cars; charging via 400V DC up to ~250 kW. MSRP starts around $81,290. Sources: https://recharged.com/articles/volvo-ex90-software-update-history, https://www.volvocars.com/us/l/north-american-charging-standard/

New Twin Motor Performance — 670 hp, the most powerful production Volvo ever. NACS port is now built in; no adapter required. Final US model year for the S90 — production at Daqing, China ended late 2024, sell-down through MY2025. PHEV (T8) dropped; B6 48V mild-hybrid is the only powertrain (295 hp, supercharged and turbocharged 2.0L, AWD standard). Trims: B6 Plus AWD ($58,300 MSRP) and B6 Ultra AWD ($63,900 MSRP). No 2026 successor. Sources: https://www.kbb.com/volvo/s90/2025/specs/, https://carbuzz.com/volvo-s90-sedan-final-year/
V60 Cross Country MY2025 sold in B5 mild-hybrid form only. Plus and Ultra trims. MSRP $50,300 (Plus) and $55,400 (Ultra). Source: https://www.cars.com/research/volvo-v60_cross_country-2025/specs/

MY2026 carries forward the B5-only MHEV powertrain across Plus and Ultra trims. Pricing rises to $52,300 (Plus) and $57,600 (Ultra). Sources: https://www.volvocars.com/us/cars/v60-cross-country/, https://www.mclaughlinvolvocars.com/volvo-v60-trim-options.htm

Naming/trim refresh. B4 (FWD only, 194 hp) becomes the new standard powertrain, replacing the prior turbo-only T-engines. B5 (AWD, 247 hp) remains the uplevel option. Trim ladder: B4 Core, B4 Plus, B5 Core, B5 Plus, B5 Ultra, B5 Ultra Black Edition. Source: https://www.media.volvocars.com/us/en-us/media/pressreleases/338590/volvo-car-usa-2025-model-year-pricing-and-change

MY2026 carries forward MY2025's trim and powertrain mix (B4 FWD MHEV / B5 AWD MHEV across Core, Plus, Ultra, Ultra Black Edition) with modest equipment refreshes and the latest Volvo Car UX OTA. Sources: https://www.volvocars.com/us/cars/xc40/, https://www.volvocarsofcary.com/2026-volvo-xc40-vs-2025-volvo-xc40.htm, https://www.empirevolvocarssmithtown.com/blog/2025/july/16/new-2026-volvo-xc40-trim-levels-explained.htm

First year of the new naming convention — 'Recharge' badge dropped, the PHEV is now XC60 T8 (was XC60 Recharge T8). Trim mix: Core, Plus, Ultra (B5 mild-hybrid or T8 PHEV) plus the top-spec T8 Polestar Engineered. PHEV gets ~35 mi EPA electric range, 18.8 kWh battery. T8 Polestar Engineered MSRP ~$75,250. Sources: https://www.edmunds.com/volvo/xc60/2025/plug-in-hybrid/, https://www.edmunds.com/volvo/xc60/2025/t8-polestar-engineered/

Substantial mid-cycle refresh. New exterior styling (revised front fascia, lighting), new interior with redesigned center console, new 11.2-inch portrait center display running the latest Volvo Car UX with Google Built-in. Powertrain options unchanged (B5 MHEV / T8 PHEV / T8 Polestar Engineered). Trim pricing rises modestly — T8 Polestar Engineered MSRP ~$79,800. Sources: https://www.volvocars.com/us/cars/xc60-hybrid/, https://www.edmunds.com/volvo/xc60/2026/, https://www.kbb.com/volvo/xc60/2026/t8-polestar-engineered/

Major refresh for the XC90 — new front-end styling, new interior, new 11.2-inch portrait display running Volvo Car UX with Google Built-in. Trim mix: Core, Plus, Ultra (B5 MHEV / B6 MHEV / T8 PHEV). T8 starts around ~$73K, B5 around $59K. Source: https://www.autonationvolvocarssanjose.com/research/2025-volvo-xc90-phev-trim-levels.htm

MY2026 carries the 2025 refresh forward with minor trim and pricing adjustments. B5 Core AWD starts ~$62,345 MSRP, B6 Core AWD ~$66,150, T8 Core AWD ~$76,200, T8 Ultra ~$83,400. Powertrains and equipment unchanged. Sources: https://www.volvocars.com/us/cars/xc90/, https://www.edmunds.com/volvo/xc90/, https://www.edmunds.com/volvo/xc90/2026/plug-in-hybrid/
